recorded.outcome:q-reflective-loader: Page decides (a). Lines 52-53: 'The private constructor stops other code from writing `new IdSequence()`, nothing more. ... `setAccessible` opens it.' Output line 47 'class: reflected == INSTANCE? false'; line 49 'enum: reflection: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Cannot reflectively create enum objects'; line 59 '`Constructor.newInstance` refuses any enum class'; reference table line 295. The says 'only stops source code from calling it' matches 'stops other code from writing new IdSequence(), nothing more'.

recorded.pass:q-counter-over-the-wire: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-counter-over-the-wire: Page decides (c). Lines 59-61: 'an enum is serialized as its name and read back with `valueOf`, so the reader gets the constant that already exists in its own JVM. Its fields don't travel.' Cross-JVM run lines 65-66: writer took 41 ids, 'reader: same constant? true, nextId() = 1'. Stem's 1,000 ids is a direct analogue.

recorded.pass:q-phase-arguments: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-phase-arguments: Page decides (a). Lines 159-165: 'illegal forward reference' error; 'When `PLACED` is built, `PAID` doesn't exist yet. Java 21's javac refuses the qualified form `OrderStatus.PAID` too'. Summary line 271: 'A constant can't name a later one in its arguments'. Minor gap: the page's example uses EnumSet.of, the quiz uses Set.of; the page attributes the error to the forward reference, not the factory, so this carries over.

recorded.outcome:q-trial-signup: Page decides (a). Lines 115-130: '`EnumSet` is mutable, and `final` fixes only the reference.' Near-identical example (`guest = Permission.READ_ONLY; guest.add(WRITE)` -> 'READ_ONLY is now [READ, WRITE]', 'auditor can write: true'); 'every user of the field holds that one set. Every role built on `READ_ONLY` can now write'.

recorded.outcome:q-phase-arguments:b: Refuted only by implication. The page never says outright that a constructor parameter of type Set<OrderStatus> is legal. Its example declares `OrderStatus(Set<OrderStatus> next)` and the only errors it reports are forward references ('javac reports five of these', line 164), which implies the parameter type is fine. The says ('only the forward references are refused') states that implication as fact.

recorded.outcome:q-trial-signup:b: Refuted only by implication. Line 129 says 'The `EnumSet.of` call ran once, when the class was initialized; every user of the field holds that one set', which puts the sharing on the field. The page never says EnumSet.of builds a new set on each call or that it does not cache, so the says' 'EnumSet.of builds a new set on each call' goes beyond what the page states.
